lesson_title: The Circular Flow: Leakages and Injections
hook_text: Your neighbourhood's money never rests. Watch where it goes after payday.
clip_script: Watch a month-end Friday. Somebody in your house worked all month — Friday evening, the pay lands. By Saturday morning it's moving: groceries at the supermarket, a trim at the barber, cement from the hardware. And every one of those businesses uses its takings to pay ITS people, who carry their pay to other counters... See it? The money never rests. It CIRCLES. Now picture that circling money as water in a channel — with three drains and three taps. Bank door: granny's deposit drains out, the bakery's mixer loan pours back in. Government door: tax drains out, teachers' salaries and tarred roads pour back. Border door: the imported laptop drains rands out, our oranges and platinum pull foreign money in. Drains winning? Quiet tills, shorter shifts. Taps winning? More spending, more hiring. That's the circular flow — the most useful diagram in economics, and it was running on your street the whole time.
visual_style: An animated aerial neighbourhood where glowing coins flow between houses and shops like water in a loop, with three labelled doors — BANK, GOVERNMENT, BORDER — each showing water draining out one side and gushing in the other.
pacing: Quick payday montage into a smooth continuous loop, three crisp door-beats, closing wide on the whole flowing neighbourhood.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read the water level.
